subtitle: Multirole aircraft · historical research dossier
introduction: Follow the visible aircraft, the organizations behind the program, and the public record linking specific observed examples. Source assertions, direct observations and unresolved questions are identified individually below.
scope: Major-system and institutional research across the cited dates. This is a conceptual overview, not an engineering teardown, complete parts list or present-day production census. People are shown only in their dated public roles.

systems.title: Airframe and wings
systems.text: The Army ODIN reference describes a central fuselage and straight, high-mounted wings. These labels identify external form; neither the illustration nor this description establishes internal structure or materials.

evidence.reference: General information / external configuration description; search-index access.

systems.title: Twin-boom tail
systems.text: Two tail booms and an elevated horizontal tail surface distinguish the external layout. DIA used the tail as one feature in its comparison of Iranian and recovered examples.

systems.title: Wheeled undercarriage
systems.text: Wheeled landing gear is visible in the examples compared by DIA. The record supports this observable category, not a specification for every production configuration.

systems.title: Observation equipment
systems.text: DIA identifies externally visible surveillance equipment in its comparison. Contemporary launch coverage also describes electro-optical observation equipment. The available observations do not identify all internal devices or establish uniformity across batches.

evidence.reference: Description of observation equipment in launch reporting.

systems.title: Ground segment
systems.text: Janes' illustrated deployment reporting shows a separate control vehicle alongside the aircraft. The ground segment is therefore presented as its own system category, without suggesting that its hardware sits inside the airframe.

evidence.reference: Image and description of the accompanying control vehicle.

timeline.title: The first-unveiling date remains disputed
timeline.text: Janes gives April 2016; the Army ODIN entry gives April 2017. The reviewed material does not resolve the discrepancy, so neither year is treated as settled.

timeline.title: Production-line inauguration reported
timeline.text: Mehr's contemporaneous gallery reports a Mohajer-6 production-line opening in Tehran on February 5, 2018. This anchors the announced production milestone; it does not measure actual output.

evidence.reference: Gallery introduction: inauguration, date and city.

timeline.title: Recovered aircraft enters the public evidence record
timeline.text: DIA compared a largely intact aircraft recovered from the Black Sea in 2022 with examples pictured in Iran and Iraq, judging their visible features indistinguishable. This is an attributed identification of particular examples.

evidence.reference: Printed page 7; report information cutoff October 27, 2022.

timeline.title: U.S. assessment and Iranian account differ
timeline.text: AP's account of the DIA briefing records the U.S. assessment of Iranian supply to Russia and Iran's position that a small number had been supplied before the invasion, with further supply denied. These positions remain separately attributed.

evidence.reference: London briefing and account of Iran's stated position; search-index text.

timeline.title: DIA expands its evidence presentation
timeline.text: DIA announced an updated report in August 2023 using recovered material and declassified imagery. Its coverage spans multiple aircraft families; an observation about one model cannot automatically populate another model's record.

evidence.reference: Announcement of expanded report and its evidentiary scope.

organizations.title: Qods Aviation Industries
organizations.text: Treasury attributes Mohajer-6 design and manufacture to QAI and records the Light Airplanes Design and Manufacturing Industries alias from mid-2020. The attribution is explicit; it is not a factory inspection.

organizations.title: Iran Aviation Industries Organization
organizations.text: Treasury places QAI under Iran Aviation Industries Organization (IAIO), within the defense ministry structure. This is institutional oversight, not a component supply relationship. IAIO should not be confused with the similarly abbreviated Aerospace Industries Organization.

organizations.title: Ministry of Defense and Armed Forces Logistics
organizations.text: MODAFL is the ministry named in Treasury's organizational account. A ministry's oversight does not establish which premises, workers or subcontractors produced an individual aircraft.

evidence.reference: Institutional placement of QAI and IAIO.

organizations.title: HESA: a sibling is not a proven manufacturer here
organizations.text: Treasury identifies QAI and HESA within IAIO's wider aviation organization. Shared institutional ownership alone does not establish that HESA assembled Mohajer-6; no such product edge is added.

evidence.reference: IAIO, QAI and HESA organization description.

people.title: Amir Hatami
people.text: Iranian defense minister at the reported production-line inauguration. Mehr identifies him as the official opening the line; that ceremonial role does not establish personal engineering authorship.

people.title: Mohammad Pakpour
people.text: IRGC Ground Forces commander identified in contemporary reporting as attending the inauguration. Attendance is public-event context, not proof of factory management.

people.title: Seyed Hojatollah Ghoreishi
people.text: QAI board chairman in Treasury's dated leadership record. Current officeholding and individual design responsibilities are not asserted.

people.title: Ghassem Damavandian
people.text: QAI managing director and board member in Treasury's record. Its October release uses the spelling Ghasem; this is a name variant, not another manufacturer.

people.title: Other named QAI board members
people.text: Treasury lists Hamidreza Sharifi-Tehrani, Reza Khaki, Majid Reza Niyazi-Angili and Vali Arlanizadeh as board members. These are historical organizational roles, not a list of product engineers.

people.title: Afshin Khajeh Fard
people.text: Treasury names him as IAIO's chief in May 2024. The documented relationship is leadership of the parent organization; product-specific technical work is not established.

manufacturing.title: Tehran: a historical production event
manufacturing.text: Mehr places the 2018 line-opening ceremony in Tehran. The exact premises, surveyed location and later operating status are unresolved. A corporate address is not substituted for a verified product factory, and no map coordinate is assigned.

evidence.reference: City and inauguration event; no precise premises established.

manufacturing.title: Manufacturer attribution has a narrower meaning
manufacturing.text: Treasury's QAI attribution does not describe internal workshare, supplier contracts, batch allocations or an exclusive final-assembly line. The network records the attributed organization while leaving facility fields empty.

evidence.reference: Manufacturer attribution; no batch-level factory allocation supplied.

assessment.title: An observed aircraft is not an entire production series
assessment.text: DIA's comparison supports an origin assessment for the pictured examples. It cannot establish a complete inventory, every variant, or continuity of production. Its October 2022 information cutoff also predates the Shahed-238 display.

evidence.reference: Report scope, cutoff and Mohajer-6 visual comparison.

assessment.title: Source dates and current status are different
assessment.text: The 2018 event report and subsequent institutional records describe different moments. They do not establish that the same line remains active today. The dossier preserves those dates instead of presenting a live factory or personnel registry.

subtitle: Jet-powered one-way aircraft · historical research dossier
introduction: Examine the public display, attributed development organization and evolving identification record. Exhibition configurations and later Russian derivative reporting remain separately scoped throughout this dossier.
scope: Exterior and major-system categories only. Displayed options are not a unified production configuration, and Russian Geran-3 findings are not an Iranian Shahed-238 parts list. Leadership and venue records are dated institutional context.

systems.title: Delta-wing airframe
systems.text: The 2023 display imagery shows a delta-wing exterior in a matte dark finish. An observed finish is not evidence of a particular coating technology or verified performance.

evidence.reference: Original analysis of exhibition imagery and visible finish.

systems.title: Jet propulsion
systems.text: The November display analysis identifies the named Shahed-238 as jet-powered. This supports the broad propulsion category; no engine model, construction detail or performance figure is inferred here.

evidence.reference: Named Shahed-238 identification and broad jet-propulsion category.

systems.title: Flight-management systems
systems.text: Public analysis discusses differing avionics configurations, but the exhibition did not establish one verified internal arrangement for all aircraft. This card represents a system category, not a located assembly or shared production design.

evidence.reference: Configuration discussion and explicit uncertainty about implementation and maturity.

systems.title: Displayed configuration options
systems.text: Three examples were displayed. The reviewed analysis leaves their testing, availability and configuration maturity uncertain. They must not be combined into a single aircraft containing every announced option.

evidence.reference: Three displayed examples and uncertainty about fielding.

timeline.title: An unnamed jet aircraft appears on film
timeline.text: Janes examined footage from a documentary premiered on September 26, 2023. The aircraft was unnamed in the trailer; the footage is a precursor observation, not a verified Shahed-238 naming date.

timeline.title: Named public display in Tehran
timeline.text: The War Zone identifies the November 19 exhibition as the public Shahed-238 display. Tasnim independently records the exhibition visit and Tehran venue. A public display establishes visibility, not serial-production output.

timeline.title: Early identification was not immediately confirmed
timeline.text: UNN interviewed forensic-institute director Oleksandr Ruvin, who said his institute's research had not established Shahed-238 use at that point. This dated absence of confirmation does not disprove later observations.

evidence.reference: Direct interview with Oleksandr Ruvin about the institute's findings at that date.

timeline.title: A Russian derivative needs its own evidence scope
timeline.text: UNN reports Ukrainian intelligence's examination of a Russian Geran-3 U-series sample. Its relationship to Shahed-238 does not make the sample's internals, suppliers or manufacturing arrangements evidence for the Iranian aircraft.

evidence.reference: Russian sample identity and distinction from Iranian design.

timeline.title: Civilian-impact investigation
timeline.text: Human Rights Watch identifies a Shahed-238 in a February 28, 2026 Dubai hotel-forecourt incident and relays local authorities' report of four injuries. The investigation concerns civilian harm, not manufacturing attribution; HRW could not rule out military guests at the hotel.

evidence.reference: Dubai hotel investigation, aircraft identification and limits.

organizations.title: Shahed Aviation Industries Research Center
organizations.text: CSIS attributes Shahed-238 development to Shahed Aviation Industries. This is a research assessment, not a manufacturer declaration or final-assembly inspection, so the supply-network development edge is conservatively marked inferred.

evidence.reference: Development attribution to Shahed Aviation Industries.

organizations.title: IRGC Aerospace Force
organizations.text: Treasury described SAIRC as subordinate to the IRGC Aerospace Force in November 2022. That institutional record predates Shahed-238's named display and cannot independently establish this model's manufacturer workshare.

evidence.reference: Shahed Aviation Industries Research Center institutional description.

organizations.title: Ashura Aerospace University
organizations.text: Tasnim identifies the university in Tehran as the exhibition venue. Its presence in the public record is as a host location; no Shahed-238 manufacturing relationship is established.

evidence.reference: Location of the IRGC Aerospace Force exhibition.

people.title: Ali Khamenei
people.text: Tasnim records his visit to the exhibition as supreme leader and commander-in-chief in November 2023. This entry describes that dated public role, not product engineering authorship or present officeholding.

evidence.reference: Exhibition visitor and public role at the event.

people.title: Amir Ali Hajizadeh
people.text: Treasury identifies Hajizadeh as IRGC Aerospace Force commander in 2019; Janes identifies him in that role in the 2023 documentary. Neither record establishes that he personally designed Shahed-238.

evidence.reference: Documentary interview participant and command role.

people.title: Saeed Aghajani
people.text: Treasury names Aghajani as IRGC Aerospace Force UAV Command commander in October 2021. This provides earlier institutional context; no product-specific Shahed-238 development role is established.

people.title: Product-specific engineers remain unverified
people.text: The reviewed development assessment names an organization, not a verified engineering team. Public commanders and exhibition attendees should not be converted into designer or supplier records.

evidence.reference: Organizational development attribution without individual engineering credits.

manufacturing.title: A Tehran exhibition venue is not a factory
manufacturing.text: The November 2023 venue establishes where the aircraft was shown. It supplies no proof of final assembly there. No military-site coordinates or factory marker are assigned.

manufacturing.title: Iranian final assembly remains unresolved
manufacturing.text: The reviewed CSIS profile does not provide independently verified, product-specific Iranian final-assembly premises or workshare. General Shahed-family manufacturing statements are insufficient to fill that gap.

evidence.reference: Development/manufacturing discussion lacks independently verified Iranian site allocation.

manufacturing.title: Geran-3 observations stay with the Russian sample
manufacturing.text: The reported Geran-3 examination concerns a distinct Russian sample. Transferring its plant, companies or hardware findings to every Iranian Shahed-238 would erase the very provenance distinctions this collection preserves.

evidence.reference: Russian sample examination and separate production context.

assessment.title: Shahed is a family name, not a shared parts list
assessment.text: Treasury's 2022 family-level account predates the named Shahed-238 display. It supports institutional background only. Shahed-131, Shahed-136 and Geran-2 claims therefore do not automatically become Shahed-238 dependencies.

assessment.title: Identification changed as evidence accumulated
assessment.text: The January 2024 interview records uncertainty at one institute at one time. Later Russian-sample reporting and HRW's 2026 identification concern different observations; none retroactively verifies every earlier claim.
